main_text.l: Sub Carolo M. regnum Francorum florentissimum fuit.

Ab hoc secunda familia Regnum Franciæ vocatur Carolingorum. Hic Carolus devictâ Germaniâ & Longobardiâ sive Italiâ, extinctam Romani Imperii in Occidente inde usq; à Romulo Momyllo Augustulo majestatem A. C. 800. iterum restituit, & Imperator Romanorum à Leone III. Pontifice Romano coronatus fuit, acclamante populo Romano: Carolo Augusto à Deo coronato Pio, Felici, vita, salus & victoria.
Plerique per Galliam, Belgium & Germaniam Principatus à Carolingis instituti.

page.notes: The marginal note at the left is written as "inde (2)Ca-rolingorum fa-milia", with the printed hyphens kept; the line-end "rolingo" may have no hyphen, which I could not confirm. "Momyllo" is a doubtful reading (possibly "Momyllo" or "Momylo"). The faint word "Sub" at the bottom left and the faint text along the right edge are show-through from the other side and are left out. The last paragraph runs off the foot of the scan at "Saxonia", so it is a fragment that continues on the next page.
